stem:
Sonia studies a snowflake drawing in which each branch tip carries a smaller copy of the same branched shape, repeated at still smaller scales. She also looks at a plain straight line segment with no smaller copies along it.

Which claim correctly decides whether the snowflake drawing is a fractal?

options.text: The snowflake drawing is a fractal because it repeats a similar branched shape at smaller scales.
The snowflake drawing is not a fractal because the branches get shorter.
The snowflake drawing is a fractal because it is drawn with straight line segments.
The plain straight line segment is a fractal because it is a simple shape.

teacher.key_rationale: A fractal shows self-similar structure at smaller scales. The snowflake drawing does; shorter branches do not cancel that, straight segments alone do not make a fractal, and the plain segment lacks smaller copies.
